tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Create a NEW module. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls, no sending, no publishing.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 8 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these — create both):
  server/pipeline/loop_tick.py
  tests/test_loop_tick.py

DO NOT EDIT server/pipeline/orchestrator.py. It is large, shared, and another lane owns it. Your module must be callable FROM the orchestrator later without the orchestrator existing yet.

SOURCE OF TRUTH: docs/SPEC-autonomous-podcast-loop.md. Read it in the worktree first.

WHY. Waves 1 and 2 built the decision modules. Nothing yet decides what the loop should DO on a given tick. This module is the brain of the autonomous loop: given the current state of the world, it returns the ordered list of actions to take. It performs none of them.

MODULES ALREADY BUILT — import and USE them; do not reimplement their logic:
  server.pipeline.pipeline_queue      queue_status, in_flight, is_stalled
  server.pipeline.candidate_vetting   evaluate_candidate, rank_candidates
  server.pipeline.send_safety         may_send
  server.pipeline.referral_lifecycle  next_action, may_contact_referred
  server.pipeline.promo_schedule      plan_week
  server.pipeline.hold_lifecycle      resume_decision, outstanding_blockers
Read each module's real signature in the worktree before calling it. If a
signature differs from this brief, follow the code and note it in a comment.

BUILD server/pipeline/loop_tick.py — stdlib plus those imports. PURE: it takes a
world snapshot and returns intended actions. It must not send, publish, write
files, or mutate the episodes it is given.

  plan_tick(world, *, now) -> dict
      `world` is a dict the caller assembles:
        {"episodes": [...], "candidates": [...], "referrals": [...],
         "recent_topics": [...], "sent_today": int, "env": {...},
         "ledger_has_key": callable}
      Returns:
        {"queue": <queue_status output>,
         "actions": [ordered action dicts],
         "escalations": [{"kind","reason"}],
         "skipped": [{"what","reason"}]}

      Each action is {"kind": str, "target": str, "payload": {...},
      "why": str}. `why` is required on every action and must reference the
      condition that produced it, so a human reading a tick log can tell why
      the loop did something.

      ORDER OF PRECEDENCE, highest first:
        1. Resume held episodes whose blockers have cleared (hold_lifecycle).
        2. Escalate if the queue is below the escalation threshold, AND in the
           same tick emit outreach actions. Never escalate without also acting:
           the owner said alert AND refill, never alert and wait.
        3. Referral actions (ask referrer for an introduction, follow up with an
           introduced person). Never emit an action targeting a referred person
           unless may_contact_referred allows it.
        4. Outreach to ranked qualified candidates, only while the in-flight
           count is below target, and only as many as the gap requires.
        5. Promotion touches due today from plan_week.

      SAFETY, non-negotiable: every action whose kind is an external send must
      be passed through send_safety.may_send. When may_send denies, the action
      does NOT appear in "actions"; it appears in "skipped" with the deny
      reason. A denied send must never silently vanish, because an invisible
      refusal looks identical to no work being needed.

      A stalled episode never produces outreach-to-guest actions; it produces an
      escalation.

      Determinism: same world and same `now` produce identical output, including
      ordering. No randomness, no wall-clock reads inside the function.

TESTS (tests/test_loop_tick.py; at least 8). Build small synthetic worlds:
 (1) a healthy world of six in-flight episodes emits no outreach and no escalation;
 (2) four in-flight emits outreach actions but no escalation;
 (3) two in-flight emits an escalation AND outreach in the same tick — assert
     both are present, since alert-without-action was explicitly rejected;
 (4) NEGATIVE and central: a referral in state "recorded" never produces an
     action targeting the referred person; the action targets the referrer;
 (5) NEGATIVE: an external-send action that may_send denies appears in
     "skipped" with the reason and NOT in "actions";
 (6) NEGATIVE: with the kill switch engaged in world["env"], no external-send
     action appears in "actions" at all, and each is recorded in "skipped";
 (7) a held episode with cleared blockers produces a resume action, and it is
     ordered before outreach;
 (8) NEGATIVE: a stalled episode produces an escalation and never a
     guest-outreach action;
 (9) every returned action carries a non-empty "why";
 (10) determinism: two identical calls return identical output.
tasks.verified: the loop's decision brain: ordered actions from a world snapshot, denied sends surfaced rather than vanishing, escalation always paired with action
